reviewer.note: Round 1 review at 8ae80984 (PR #457, front-gable roofs), docs/reviews/2026-11-10-front-gable-roofs.md. Verdict for these bytes (58a678d2...). Fail. Rakes, boards, ridge, finial and band as on the library (2,1,2,1, 0 breaks; board 9 texels; back-edge breaks only where the stack stands). Faults: 28 flat 2x2 #2e2943 nail heads on the lapped gable, none lit, on an exact 36-texel grid (GR2); the 'low' stack's foot has no readable apron, soakers or contact shadow (GR3). Light consistent; stack faces lit west / dark east. Polish GR4, GR5, GR6, GR8.
fix_list: GR2 (fault): the lapped-board gable's nail heads are flat one-tone 2x2 #2e2943 squares with no lit texel, on an exact grid (x every 36 texels, one on every board). As XR3-S1: give each head one lit #737078 texel at its upper left and a dark texel under-right so it sits in the board, jitter positions by 1-2 texels, skip about one board in four, and keep the lit texel through tidy with finish(keep=).

GR3 (fault): the stack's foot has no readable apron, soakers or contact shadow. Today 11-14 lead texels per house (#888697, #696e87): a 4-texel column on the west side and a 5-10 texel cluster at the downhill corner; along the rest of the foot the stack's stones meet the slope's course highlights (#333051, #4e4f6d) directly, and no slate below the foot is stepped down. Draw a lead apron along the whole foot, 2 texels deep, stepping with the courses: top row lit lead, lower row the lead's dark where it turns down the slope; one soaker texel column up each side (the east one a step darker); and the contact shadow as the course highlights removed (#333051/#4e4f6d to #1a1233) for 3-4 texels below the apron and 2 texels east of the east face. Check it at 1x and 2x in the street.

GR4 (polish): make the gable band's 2-texel line continuous. In 8-25 % of rake columns a texel at the wall's own body or lit tone sits in rows 1-2 under the board (library x 208: #a69c8e right under the board; x 53: #988e85), and on stone gables the fade (rows 3-5, 19-39 % darker) is nearly as dark as the line (36-49 %), so it reads as one 5-texel band. B5 has a continuous line about 72 % darker and a fade of 33 and 20 %. Rows 1-2: no texel above 0.55 of the gable wall's median; rows 3-5: about 18 %.

GR5 (polish): the west end grain at the left foot is the board's body tone (#8e6242, col 0), not lit; make it #a87c52 with a 2-texel ring arc. The feet now touch canvas columns 0 and W-1: keep 1 texel of transparent margin.

GR6 (polish): calm the slopes. Roof-only cluster noise 41.2-43.5 %; the shaded slope carries 13.5-18.8 tones and 25.6-31.3 shapes a 16x16 patch (through the reference pipeline) against 3.0 and 4.7 on B5's shaded plane. Keep the course lines on the shaded slope and drop most per-slate highlights (about 1 in 3 left).
GR8 (polish): the lapped boards' grain is scattered 1-2 texel dark dashes over every board and reads as speckle at 2x; group it into 2-3 streaks a board that wander and end.
